title: Target anatomy
view: Transverse section of the right distal leg about 7 cm above the lateral malleolus, under a probe on the anterolateral leg, as on ultrasound: lateral (peroneus brevis, fibula) on the image left, anterior (EDL) on the right. Composition after NYSORA's plate (concept only), mirrored to the house laterality.
teachingPoint: The nerve lies just deep to the crural fascia where the septum between the peroneal and extensor compartments meets it; the needle comes in-plane from anterior and the spread surrounds the nerve under the fascia.
claims: Distal third of the right leg in section, lateral on the left (record: distal third of the lateral leg; NYSORA 5-10 cm above the lateral malleolus).
Nerve at the junction of the crural fascia and the septum between peroneus brevis and extensor digitorum longus, just deep to the fascia (record anatomy; NYSORA).
Fibula deep in the lateral compartment; muscles packed with thin septa (standard anatomy).
Needle in-plane from the anterior side, tip beside the nerve under the fascia (record step 3; NYSORA in-plane).
Teal: spread around the nerve under the fascia (record step 4).
Labels: Crural fascia, Superficial peroneal nerve, Peroneus brevis, Extensor digitorum longus, Fibula.
